title: Execution & Restoration Adventure
welcome_lead: On 30 January 1649, England did something amazing: it executed its king. Then it tried life without one. 👑
meta_desc: Execution Adventure — a KS3 walkthrough of the execution of Charles I, the Commonwealth and the Restoration.
final_note: You saw the trial of Charles I, the Commonwealth, Cromwell's rule and the return of the king in 1660.

concepts.def: Strict Protestant who disliked fancy ceremony
Return of Charles II as king in 1660

walkthroughs.body_html:
After Charles I started a second war in 1648, the army had had enough.

Parliament put him on trial for treason. He refused to defend himself — he said no court could judge a king.

On 30 January 1649, Charles was beheaded outside Whitehall in London. Witnesses said a deep groan went up from the crowd. ⚰️

Parliament abolished the monarchy and the House of Lords. England became a Commonwealth — a republic.

The army got fed up with Parliament. In 1653, Cromwell took the title Lord Protector. He ruled almost like a king, but without a crown.

Strict Puritan rules followed: theatres closed, Christmas celebrations banned, swearing fined. Many people hated it. 🎄❌

Cromwell died in 1658. His son Richard tried to rule but quickly failed.

In 1660, Parliament invited Charles II back from exile. This is called the Restoration.

The monarchy was restored, but it was now clear: no king could ignore Parliament. Cromwell's body was even dug up and 'executed' as revenge!
